hero.headline: Justice Department Clears Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros.
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has approved the $111 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, removing a major regulatory obstacle for one of the entertainment industry's largest consolidations. The decision came after an eight-month investigation by the Justice Department's antitrust division, which examined whether the combination would harm competition.

The combined company will bring together Paramount's assets, including CBS, Paramount Pictures, and Paramount+, with Warner Bros. Discovery's properties such as HBO, Max, CNN, and the Warner Bros. film studio. According to the Justice Department, "the transaction is not likely to result in harm to competition or American consumers" in streaming video, linear television, or theatrical film production and distribution.

The merger represents a significant industry bet that scale will prove essential in the streaming era. Both companies have faced competitive pressures as they compete against dominant technology platforms. The combined entity is expected to pursue approximately $6 billion in cost savings through operational synergies.

However, the deal still faces additional regulatory hurdles. The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has opened its own investigation with a July deadline to determine whether a more thorough review is needed. European regulators are also examining the funding behind the merger, which includes $24 billion in commitments from Gulf-based sovereign wealth funds. Australia has already approved the transaction.

The merger has generated significant opposition from media critics and politicians. Senator Elizabeth Warren called the approval "terrible news for every American who doesn't want Trump-aligned billionaires to control what they watch and how much they pay." Craig Aaron, co-chief executive of Free Press, stated that the investigation appeared predetermined, saying "the fix was in at the Trump Justice Department from the start."

Journalists at CBS News and CNN have expressed particular concerns about potential integration of the two newsrooms, which would likely result in significant job cuts given the promised cost savings. Some CNN staff have worried about editorial direction changes following the merger. David Ellison, who will control the combined company, pledged in March that CNN's editorial independence would be protected.

California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, indicated his office continues investigating the deal. A coalition of state attorneys general could still file a lawsuit to block the merger in coming weeks, potentially led by Bonta's office.

Paramount defended the merger in a statement, calling it "pro-competitive" and saying it would create "a stronger company better positioned to compete against dominant technology platforms." The company expressed commitment to completing the transaction while the remaining regulatory reviews proceed.

cards.headline: Trump Announces Iran Peace Deal Signing for Sunday as Tehran Disputes Timeline
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran would be signed on Sunday, but Iranian officials quickly cast doubt on the timeline, saying no final decision has been reached on when such a signing might occur.

Trump made the announcement through a social media post, claiming the deal would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping. However, Iran's foreign ministry offered a different timeline, suggesting an agreement could be finalized in the coming days but that Sunday would not be the signing date.

The conflicting statements highlight the tension surrounding weeks of halting negotiations. A senior US official suggested there was an 80 to 85 percent likelihood of an agreement being signed within days, but acknowledged that internal divisions within Iran's leadership were complicating the process.

"Most of the people that we've been speaking to, and most of the people who have authority within their system, want to sign this deal, but not everybody," the official said. "And those internal fractures are sort of working themselves out."

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said an agreement on addressing what Tehran calls the US-Israeli war against Iran had "never been closer," but urged media outlets to avoid speculating about its contents until it was finalized. Iran's state news agency confirmed that "the broad outlines" of a deal were being finalized.

However, significant disagreements remain on key issues. The Strait of Hormuz has been a major point of contention. Iran shut the waterway to most shipping after the conflict began in February, wanting to levy tolls on vessels passing through. The US has insisted that Tehran restore freedom of navigation through the crucial waterway, which carries a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied gas supplies.

US officials said the agreement stipulates that the strait would open and the US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. But Iranian state media claimed the deal would not require Iran to give up control of the strait.

The disagreements extend to other major issues as well. Iranian news agencies published a supposed draft claiming the deal would release 24 billion dollars of Iran's frozen assets, suspend sanctions on oil sales, include US reparations, and dismantle Iran's nuclear program. US officials countered that the agreement would require Iran's nuclear material to be destroyed, with no frozen money released until Tehran met certain demands, and that Iran would stop supporting militant movements.

Trump has repeatedly claimed in recent weeks that a deal was on the point of completion, only to revert to threatening Iran with attacks. The uncertainty over the signing date suggests that significant details remain under negotiation, with both governments facing domestic and international pressure to resolve the conflict.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Imposes Export Controls on Anthropic AI Models
cards.teaser: The White House restricted access to Anthropic's latest AI models after Amazon executives raised concerns with U.S. officials.
cards.body:
The U.S. government ordered Anthropic to suspend access to its most advanced AI models—Fable 5 and Mythos 5—for foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. Anthropic said it received the export control directive without being given specific details about the security threat, and announced it would "abruptly disable" these models for all users in response.

The government believes safeguards in the models can be bypassed and the technology could be used to identify software vulnerabilities. Amazon executives had raised concerns about Anthropic's models before the government action, according to sources familiar with the matter.

cards.headline: White House imposed export controls on Anthropic AI model after Amazon alert
cards.teaser: The White House imposed emergency export controls on Anthropic's advanced AI model after a series of urgent calls between the company's CEO and administration o.
cards.body:
The White House imposed emergency export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models following cybersecurity research from Amazon and conversations between Anthropic CEO Andy Jassy and administration officials. The powerful models had been publicly available for only days before the administration ordered them removed.

The rapid intervention underscores the White House's hands-on approach to managing advanced AI capabilities. The episode marks one of the most direct federal interventions in controlling access to AI technology, with the administration responding to developments as they emerge rather than through established regulatory frameworks.

cards.headline: Pentagon Adds Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD to Chinese Military Company List
cards.teaser: The Defense Department designated three of China's largest companies as supporters of the Chinese military, drawing sharp criticism from Beijing.
cards.body:
The Pentagon updated its list of Chinese military companies to include Alibaba, Baidu, and BYD, claiming these major firms support China's armed forces. The designation can restrict U.S. companies from conducting business with the listed entities and marks a significant expansion to encompass prominent commercial brands.

The timing of the announcement comes less than a month after Donald Trump visited Beijing and met with Xi Jinping to maintain a trade war truce. China's government has rebuked the United States over the military designations of its top firms.

cards.headline: Meta begins dismantling $2 billion Manus acquisition after Beijing demands reversal
cards.body:
Meta has started unwinding its $2 billion acquisition of Manus following a directive from Beijing ordering the deal reversed. The social media company is now working to dismantle the transaction, which had been one of its largest recent acquisitions.

The reversal comes after Chinese authorities intervened to block the deal. Manus, the company at the center of the acquisition, had been purchased by Meta as part of its expansion strategy. Beijing's demand for the deal's reversal represents a direct intervention in a major American tech transaction.

The move highlights ongoing tensions between Chinese regulatory authorities and American technology companies operating in or seeking to expand into Chinese markets. For Meta, which has faced regulatory scrutiny in multiple jurisdictions, the forced unwinding represents a significant setback to its strategic plans. The $2 billion price tag made the Manus acquisition one of the company's more substantial recent investments.

The process of dismantling an acquisition of this scale involves complex legal and financial steps. Meta will need to reverse ownership structures, potentially unwind integrated operations, and address contractual obligations created during the merger process. The timeline for completing the unwinding has not been disclosed.

This development adds to a growing list of instances where Chinese regulatory intervention has affected American tech companies' business plans. The forced reversal of a completed $2 billion acquisition demonstrates Beijing's willingness to exercise authority over deals involving companies that operate within or have ties to Chinese markets, even when those deals involve major American corporations.

cards.headline: U.S. Power Demand Set to Break Records as AI Use Surges
cards.teaser: American electricity consumption will reach record highs in 2026 and 2027, driven by surging demand from artificial intelligence data centers.
cards.body:
U.S. power usage is projected to exceed record levels in 2026 and 2027 as artificial intelligence applications drive unprecedented electricity demand, according to the Energy Information Administration. The surge is forcing AI companies to pursue creative solutions as they compete for limited energy supplies, with data center construction outpacing power infrastructure development.

The energy decisions being made now could shape economic and environmental outcomes for the next century. AI firms are scrambling to secure electricity access for data centers that power their systems. The Pacific Northwest National Laboratory has compiled comprehensive guidance for data center construction as the industry races to build capacity.

cards.headline: Swiss Vote on Proposal to Cap Population at 10 Million
cards.teaser: Switzerland is holding a referendum on whether to impose a population cap, with voters deciding if the country should limit growth.
cards.body:
Swiss voters are deciding on a far-right proposal to limit the country's population to 10 million. If approved, the government would be required to implement restrictions on family reunification, residency permits, and asylum by 2050, with measures potentially triggered earlier if the population reaches 9.5 million.

Supporters of the initiative frame it as a sustainability measure, while opponents warn it would devastate Switzerland's economy and international reputation. The ballot concludes this weekend.

cards.headline: Indian Officials Criticize US for Lack of Condolences After Strike Kills Sailors
cards.teaser: Indian politician Shashi Tharoor said the US offered no condolences after American strikes near Oman killed Indian sailors.
cards.body:
Indian politician Shashi Tharoor expressed shock that the United States, which he described as a friend to India, did not offer condolences following the deaths of Indian sailors in a US strike near Oman. The strike occurred during American military operations connected to the Iran conflict.

The incident has drawn anger in India as families mourn the crew members killed. One sailor, Patnala Suresh, had reassured his wife before the strike that he would return home safely. The couple had been planning to celebrate their 15th wedding anniversary that month. The absence of official US acknowledgment has fueled criticism regarding American military activities in the Persian Gulf region.

cards.headline: Top Haitian Security Official Kidnapped
cards.teaser: A security expert who recently became chief of staff to Haiti's defense minister was abducted in the latest example of violence in the country.
cards.body:
A high-ranking Haitian security official was kidnapped, according to reports from the country. The victim had recently been appointed chief of staff to the new defense minister.

The abduction represents the latest incident in ongoing violence that has gripped Haiti. Security conditions in the country have deteriorated significantly, with kidnappings becoming increasingly common even among government officials and security personnel.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills One in Southern Russia, Hits Sea Terminal
cards.teaser: A Ukrainian drone attack on southern Russia killed one person and triggered a fire at a sea terminal.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces conducted a drone strike in southern Russia that killed one person and injured three others. The attack also triggered a fire at a sea terminal in the region.

Ukraine has stated it will continue targeting Russian energy infrastructure following the strike. Russian officials reported that the attack hit facilities in the Volgograd region. Satellite imagery has shown Russia wrapping buildings in anti-drone cages to protect infrastructure, though Ukraine subsequently targeted at least one such protected facility with cruise missiles.

cards.headline: Canada's Carney Calls for Unity with EU Before G7 Summit
cards.teaser: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged cooperation among middle-power countries ahead of the G7 meeting.
cards.body:
Mark Carney called for Canada and the European Union to present a united front before the upcoming G7 summit. The Canadian prime minister has been softening his tone toward President Trump as trade negotiations continue.

Carney said middle-power countries should not compete for favor with the United States. His comments come as Canada navigates complex trade discussions, with the US reportedly wanting to avoid a congressional vote on any trade deal. The G7 summit represents a key moment for Carney to position Canada among allied nations.

cards.headline: Nigerian Author Accuses Hospital of Stalling Review into Son's Death
cards.teaser: A Nigerian author says a Lagos hospital is trying to prevent an inquest into the death of her 21-month-old son.
cards.body:
Renowned Nigerian author Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has accused a Lagos hospital of attempting to obstruct an official inquiry into her son's death. Her child, aged 21 months, died while receiving treatment at the medical facility.

Adichie is pressing for a formal inquest to examine the circumstances surrounding her son's death at the hospital, which she claims is working to prevent the review from proceeding.

hero.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from facade following court rulings
hero.body:
Workers removed Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade in Washington, D.C., after the performing arts venue missed a federal judge's deadline to complete the task. The removal began in the early hours of Saturday, following a judge's rejection of an emergency appeal to block the work.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper had ordered the Kennedy Center to remove all references to "Trump Kennedy Center" by Friday at 11:59 p.m. local time. Crews had erected scaffolding on Friday as onlookers gathered into the evening, though storms delayed the removal work until the following morning. The actual removal then proceeded behind a screen.

The building's exterior had displayed "The Donald J Trump and The John F Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts" as of Monday afternoon, before the work began. Following the removal, the facility will be known as "The John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts" or simply the "Kennedy Center."

In his 94-page ruling, Judge Cooper determined that the Kennedy Center's organic statute makes clear the institution is named for President Kennedy and cannot bear any other formal name or public memorial without congressional action. "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it," Cooper wrote.

The judge's order also addressed a broader dispute over the venue's governance. Trump's handpicked board had previously approved a $257 million "revitalization project" that would have closed the center for two years. Cooper temporarily blocked this renovation plan as part of his decision.

The Kennedy Center's general counsel issued a memo directing employees to immediately change email signatures, letterheads, and other documents to remove Trump's name. The deadline for completing changes to templates, forms, signage, brochures, and website pages was set for June 12, 2026.

The removal of Trump's name represents a significant change to the visual identity of one of Washington's most recognizable landmarks along the city's monumental core. The Kennedy Center operates as a federally chartered organization that also receives private donations and functions as the nation's cultural center and memorial to President John F. Kennedy.

Following the judge's decision, Trump responded with a lengthy statement on social media, expressing his position on the matter and the legal proceedings. The dispute centered on questions about the institution's authority to modify naming agreements and building signage based on its governing structure and governance guidelines.

cards.headline: Texas Republicans add bans on IVF and Sharia law to party platform
cards.teaser: The Texas Republican Party adopted new platform provisions at its state convention, including language seeking bans on in vitro fertilization and Sharia law.
cards.body:
The Texas Republican Party approved additions to its official platform at the state convention that call for prohibiting in vitro fertilization and Sharia law. The platform changes come as the party also saw leadership transitions, with party chair Abraham George losing his reelection bid at the gathering.

Texas Governor and other Republican leaders, including Attorney General Ken Paxton, urged party unity during the convention. The platform additions reflect positions that party delegates voted to include as official policy stances, though state platforms do not carry the force of law and serve primarily as statements of party priorities and values.

cards.headline: Pentagon releases new batch of UFO files including orb sightings
cards.teaser: The White House released a third batch of unidentified flying object records through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters.
cards.body:
The Department of War made public additional files documenting unidentified aerial phenomena encounters, including reports of glowing red orbs and videos of mysterious objects. The release marks the third batch of UFO records made available through the formal reporting system established for documenting such sightings.

The newly released files include reports from Colorado describing objects characterized as resembling a potato hovering in the sky. The records also contain videos showing orb-like objects and documentation from military and civilian observers. The Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, known by the acronym PURSUE, serves as the official channel for making these historical reports available to the public.

cards.headline: Live elephant brought to Texas GOP convention urinates on convention floor
cards.teaser: A live elephant brought to the Texas Republican Party convention urinated in the middle of the event venue.
cards.body:
A 4-ton African elephant named Paige was brought to the Texas Republican Party's state convention in Houston as a surprise for attendees. The elephant made her appearance after Governor Greg Abbott completed his keynote speech on Friday, with organizers having warned convention-goers to keep the aisles clear for a "larger-than-life surprise."

The elephant urinated on the convention floor, drawing widespread attention and raising animal welfare concerns. The incident became a widely discussed moment from the multi-day convention, which also featured platform debates and leadership elections.

cards.headline: Ticketmaster reassures Knicks fans after website message causes panic
cards.teaser: Ticketmaster issued a statement clarifying that New York Knicks fans will be able to access an upcoming game after a confusing note on its website sparked concern.
cards.body:
A note on Ticketmaster's website sparked confusion and concern among New York Knicks fans seeking to purchase game tickets. The message triggered backlash among ticketholders who worried about access issues.

Ticketmaster moved quickly to reassure supporters, confirming that fans would not be locked out of attending the game. The company's statement addressed the panic that had spread among Knicks supporters following the appearance of the website message.

cards.headline: Trump claims Iran no longer seeks nuclear weapon as peace deal talks continue
cards.teaser: President Trump stated that Iran no longer wants to develop nuclear weapons, making claims about Iranian intentions as negotiations over a peace agreement proceed.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that a peace agreement with Iran would be signed on Sunday, declaring that the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened to all traffic immediately after. He also claimed Iran no longer wants nuclear weapons. Trump cancelled planned missile strikes against Iran following two days of escalating attacks that had threatened the ceasefire.

However, Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's timeline, stating that no final decision on an agreement had been reached. Both sides and their mediators expressed cautious optimism that weeks of halting negotiations were approaching a conclusion, though the parties remained publicly at odds over the deal's status.

cards.headline: Trump and Iran dispute timeline for signing peace agreement
cards.teaser: President Trump said a peace deal with Iran will be signed on a specific day, but Iranian officials pushed back on that timeline.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that the United States and Iran would sign a peace agreement, stating it could be completed by Sunday. He also canceled planned missile strikes on Iran following two days of escalating attacks that had threatened the ceasefire between the nations.

Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's timeline, saying no final decision on an agreement had been reached. The announcement came through Trump's social media posts, rather than formal diplomatic channels, highlighting the ongoing tensions between the two governments over the terms and timing of any potential deal.

cards.teaser: Multiple state attorneys general have launched an investigation into OpenAI, focusing on ChatGPT's impact on young users.
cards.body:
A coalition of state attorneys general is investigating OpenAI, according to reports from the Wall Street Journal. The investigation examines multiple aspects of the company's operations, including its advertising policies and handling of health data.

OpenAI stated it is cooperating with the state attorneys general and welcomes the opportunity to address their concerns. The investigation reflects broader regulatory scrutiny as government officials work to understand the implications of rapidly advancing artificial intelligence technology.

cards.headline: Stock Market Holds Steady Following SpaceX IPO
cards.teaser: Markets absorbed the largest initial public offering ever as SpaceX stock jumped nearly 30 percent, pushing Elon Musk's net worth past one trillion dollars.
cards.body:
SpaceX made its historic debut on the Nasdaq, raising $75 billion in what became a record-breaking initial public offering. The company's valuation reached $2.1 trillion following its first day of trading, with shares climbing nearly 30 percent in early sessions.

The offering significantly boosted Elon Musk's personal wealth, pushing his net worth to $1.1 trillion and making him the world's first trillionaire. His fortune increased by more than $62 billion from the previous day as SpaceX shares soared. Musk maintained control of the company's voting structure, giving him substantial influence over the newly public firm's direction.

cards.headline: Debate Emerges Over How to Tax Artificial Intelligence
cards.teaser: Bernie Sanders, President Trump, and AI companies agree the public should share in AI wealth, but their proposed solutions differ sharply.
cards.body:
Political leaders and artificial intelligence companies increasingly agree that the public should benefit from AI-generated wealth. Bernie Sanders, President Trump, and major AI firms have all endorsed sharing the technology's economic gains more broadly.

However, significant disagreement exists over how to implement this goal. Proposed approaches vary across the political spectrum, including direct taxes on AI companies, levies on AI-generated products and services, or entirely new tax structures designed to capture value from the technology.

cards.headline: KPMG retracts AI usage report citing hallucinations in data
cards.teaser: The consulting firm withdrew its report on artificial intelligence usage after discovering the AI tools used had generated unreliable information.
cards.body:
KPMG has pulled a report analyzing AI usage patterns after determining that the findings contained hallucinations generated by artificial intelligence tools. The consulting firm acknowledged that AI had produced unreliable information about AI itself, undermining the credibility of the report's conclusions.

The incident adds to growing concerns about the reliability of AI-generated content, particularly when AI systems are used to analyze or report on artificial intelligence technology. Hallucinations occur when AI systems generate plausible-sounding but factually incorrect information, a known limitation of current language models.

cards.headline: Amazon CEO raised concerns about Anthropic models before access cutoff
cards.teaser: Andy Jassy reportedly flagged security issues with Anthropic models that led to the company restricting worldwide access to two of its AI systems.
cards.body:

The government ordered the company to suspend access for foreign nationals, citing national security concerns and claiming the models' safeguards can be bypassed to identify software vulnerabilities.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy may have raised initial security concerns about these models before the government action. Anthropic, which has received investment from Amazon, said it received the directive without being given specific details about the national security threat.

cards.headline: OpenAI under investigation by state attorneys general
cards.teaser: Multiple state attorneys general are examining OpenAI's practices, including its advertising policies and handling of health data.
cards.body:
State attorneys general are investigating OpenAI, focusing on the company's advertising policies and how it handles health data. The specific states involved in the inquiry have not been identified.

The investigation is the latest regulatory action targeting OpenAI as the company expands its AI offerings. Depending on what investigators find, the probe could result in enforcement actions, policy changes, or settlements.

cards.headline: NASA revises Artemis lunar lander plans
cards.teaser: The space agency has updated its approach to the lunar lander that will carry astronauts to the moon's surface as part of the Artemis program.
cards.body:
NASA has unveiled revised plans for its Artemis lunar lander program as it advances toward crewed moon missions. The agency recently announced the crew members who will participate in the Artemis program, though these astronauts will not be landing on the lunar surface or traveling near it at this stage.

The updated lander design reflects NASA's ongoing efforts to finalize the spacecraft's technical specifications and procedures needed for eventual moon landings as part of the broader Artemis initiative.

cards.headline: Bungie releases final update for Destiny 2
cards.teaser: The game developer has delivered its last content update for the long-running shooter, marking the end of new development for the franchise.
cards.body:
Bungie has released what it calls the final update for Destiny 2, bringing new development on the game to a close. The update includes the Monument of Triumph and has driven player counts to their highest levels in two years, surpassing the all-time peak of Bungie's upcoming game Marathon.

Destiny 2 players can claim a free Deadlands cosmetics bundle as part of the final update. The game will remain playable, but Bungie will no longer produce new content updates or expansions for the title as the studio shifts focus to other projects.

cards.headline: Apple ends software support for 16 devices
cards.teaser: The company has discontinued update support for four popular product lines, affecting 16 devices total as it phases out older hardware.
cards.body:
Apple has ended software support for 16 devices across its product lineup, including iPhones, iPads, and Macs. The discontinued support means these devices will no longer receive operating system updates or security patches starting this fall.

The list includes four popular device categories that Apple has now designated as legacy products. MacBook Pro models are among the affected devices, part of Apple's regular cycle of phasing out support for older hardware as it focuses resources on current product lines.

hero.headline: Vinicius Jr scores late equalizer as Brazil draws Morocco 1-1 in World Cup opener
hero.body:
Brazil opened its 2026 World Cup campaign with a 1-1 draw against Morocco at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Vinicius Jr scored a spectacular solo goal to rescue a point for the five-time champions after Morocco had taken the lead earlier in the match.

The result leaves Brazil with work to do in Group C after a performance that raised questions about the team's overall quality beyond individual moments of brilliance. Morocco controlled significant portions of the match and appeared set to claim a historic opening victory over Brazil before Vinicius Jr's intervention.

The Real Madrid forward's goal was a moment of individual quality that highlighted the gap between Brazil's star talent and the team's collective performance. Morocco's tactics proved effective for much of the match, putting pressure on Brazil's defense and creating opportunities throughout.

Brazil entered the tournament as one of the favorites, but the opening draw suggests the path to a sixth World Cup title may be more difficult than anticipated. The team's reliance on individual brilliance from players like Vinicius Jr to salvage results could prove problematic as the tournament progresses against stronger opposition.

Both teams will look to build on the result in their next Group C matches. For Morocco, the draw represents a strong start and proof their game plan can trouble traditional powerhouses. For Brazil, the performance will prompt tactical adjustments as they seek to establish the dominance expected of a title contender. The draw leaves the group wide open heading into the second round of matches.

cards.headline: Scotland takes lead against Haiti in World Cup Group C opener
cards.teaser: John McGinn scored to give Scotland a 1-0 advantage against Haiti at Boston Stadium.
cards.body:
John McGinn put Scotland ahead 1-0 against Haiti in their opening Group C match at the Boston Stadium. The goal gave Scotland an early advantage as they began their World Cup campaign.

The match marked Haiti's first World Cup appearance and Scotland's return to the tournament. Both teams entered the match seeking a strong start in a group that also includes Brazil and Morocco.

cards.headline: Knicks and Spurs meet in NBA Finals Game 5 with series tied
cards.teaser: The NBA Finals return to San Antonio for Game 5 after the Knicks rallied from 29 points down to even the series.
cards.body:
The Knicks visit San Antonio for Game 5 of the NBA Finals with a 3-1 series lead. New York can clinch its first championship since 1973 with a victory tonight.

The Spurs' defense has been a key factor throughout the series, disrupting the Knicks' offense in crucial stretches. The game takes place at the Frost Bank Center, with country singer Mickey Guyton performing the national anthem.

cards.headline: Technical fault delays VAR offside images in Qatar-Switzerland World Cup match
cards.teaser: FIFA attributed the delayed release of VAR images to a technical fault following a disputed offside call in the Qatar-Switzerland draw.
cards.body:
FIFA blamed a technical fault for delaying the release of VAR images following a controversial offside decision in Qatar's World Cup draw with Switzerland. The incident sparked questions about the reliability of the video assistant referee system at the tournament.

The match ended 1-1 after Miro Muheim scored an own goal in stoppage time, heading into his own net under pressure from a Qatar player. This cancelled out Breel Embolo's first-half penalty for Switzerland. The result left Group B evenly poised, with all teams holding one point each.

cards.headline: Khamzat Chimaev faces Dillon Danis in RAF 10 wrestling event
cards.teaser: Khamzat Chimaev and Dillon Danis headline the RAF 10 wrestling card.
cards.body:
Khamzat Chimaev and Dillon Danis met in the main event of RAF 10, a wrestling competition featuring mixed martial arts fighters. The event drew attention due to the personalities involved and the crossover appeal of wrestlers competing outside traditional MMA.

Tensions escalated during the pre-fight press conference when Chimaev challenged Danis to a street fight. Ben Askren was also accused by Danis of avoiding him during the heated presser, adding to the drama surrounding the event.

cards.headline: Former NFL linebacker Aldon Smith dies at 36
cards.teaser: Aldon Smith, who became the fastest player to reach 30 sacks in NFL history, has died.
cards.body:
Former NFL defensive end Aldon Smith died Saturday at age 36. The San Francisco 49ers announced his death without disclosing the cause. Smith was selected seventh overall in the 2011 draft and spent six seasons in the NFL playing for the 49ers, Oakland Raiders, and Dallas Cowboys.

During his time with San Francisco, Smith earned Pro Bowl selection and All-Pro honors. The 49ers and Raiders released statements mourning his passing.

cards.headline: Tommy Fury defeats Eddie Hall by majority decision in exhibition bout
cards.teaser: Tommy Fury won a majority decision over Eddie Hall in their Misfits Boxing match before chaos erupted in the ring.
cards.body:
Tommy Fury edged Eddie Hall by majority decision in their heavyweight exhibition bout for Misfits Boxing. The match was designated as an exhibition contest due to the significant weight difference between the two fighters.

Chaos erupted in the ring following the decision. The bout drew attention due to the crossover appeal of Fury, a professional boxer, facing Hall, a former strongman competitor, in what was billed as a beauty versus beast matchup.

hero.headline: U.S. Men's Soccer World Cup Win Draws Record English-Language Viewership
hero.body:
The United States men's national soccer team's victory over Paraguay in the 2026 World Cup drew nearly 16 million viewers on Fox Sports, making it the most-watched USMNT World Cup telecast in English-language history. The match aired Friday as part of the opening round of the tournament.

The record-breaking viewership marks a significant milestone for soccer broadcasting in the United States. Fox Sports reported the audience figures as part of what the network described as a strong start to World Cup coverage. The 2026 World Cup is being co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico, with matches taking place across all three countries.

Telemundo also reported historic numbers for Spanish-language World Cup coverage. The network said the match between Mexico and South Africa became the biggest World Cup telecast in Spanish-language history, though specific viewership numbers were not provided in the announcement.

The tournament represents the first time the World Cup has returned to the United States since 1994. The multi-nation hosting arrangement and home-field advantage for the U.S. team appear to be driving increased American interest in the competition. The USMNT's strong opening performance and the resulting television ratings suggest broadcasters may see sustained high viewership throughout the tournament.

The previous English-language USMNT World Cup viewership record was not specified in the announcement, but the nearly 16 million viewers represents a substantial audience for soccer in a country where the sport has historically struggled to match the popularity of American football, basketball, and baseball. The figures reflect growing interest in soccer among U.S. audiences and the appeal of a major international tournament featuring the home team.

cards.headline: ABC New York Anchor Bill Ritter Steps Down After Alzheimer's Diagnosis
cards.teaser: Longtime WABC anchor Bill Ritter announced an early-stage Alzheimer's diagnosis on air and said he would step down from his anchoring duties.
cards.body:
Bill Ritter, who has anchored the main evening news at WABC since 2001, announced his retirement after disclosing an early-stage Alzheimer's diagnosis. The veteran broadcaster made the announcement publicly on air, sharing his diagnosis with the millions of New York viewers he has served throughout his career.

Ritter said his life had taken a turn, prompting his decision to step down from his anchoring duties. Despite retiring from his on-air role, he indicated he would continue to report on the disease.

cards.headline: Seth Rogen Says He Has No Plans to Work With James Franco Again
cards.teaser: Actor Seth Rogen told The New York Times he has not spoken to James Franco in a long time and does not plan to work with him in the future.
cards.body:
Seth Rogen said in a New York Times interview that he has not spoken to James Franco in a long time and has no plans to collaborate with the actor in the future. When asked about his relationship with Franco, Rogen acknowledged the nuance of the situation but did not elaborate further.

The comments follow allegations of sexual misconduct against Franco. Rogen and Franco had worked together on multiple films over the years, making them frequent collaborators in Hollywood before their professional relationship ended.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Apologizes to Bono for Refusing Song License for Gap Commercial
cards.teaser: Bruce Springsteen told Bono he should have approved use of his song for a Gap commercial supporting Bono's AIDS foundation.
cards.body:
Bruce Springsteen apologized to Bono for refusing to license his song Girls in Their Summer Clothes for a Gap commercial that would have supported the AIDS foundation RED. Springsteen made the apology while receiving the Harry Belafonte Voices for Social Justice Award at the Tribeca Festival, telling Bono he should have done it.

Bono presented Springsteen with the award and gave the musician a hard time about the refusal during his remarks. The commercial was intended as a partnership between the clothing brand Gap and Bono's AIDS charity organization.

cards.headline: Amy Adams Says She Rejected Graphic SNL Sketch to Protect Young Fans
cards.teaser: Amy Adams said she turned down a sketch idea from Andy Samberg while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2008 because of young viewers who had watched Enchanted.
cards.body:
During an appearance on Late Night With Seth Meyers, Amy Adams revealed that she turned down a sketch idea from Andy Samberg while hosting Saturday Night Live in 2008. The actress declined the "graphic" concept out of concern for young viewers who were fans of her film Enchanted, which had come out just months before.

Adams discussed the rejected sketch during her interview but didn't elaborate on its specific details. Her decision reflected her awareness of the young audience that Enchanted had attracted and what material she felt comfortable performing on the late-night comedy show.

cards.headline: Keke Palmer and Hot Ones Host Sean Evans Spotted on New York City Date
cards.teaser: Keke Palmer and Sean Evans were seen having dinner together at an Italian restaurant in New York City, fueling speculation about a relationship.
cards.body:
Keke Palmer and Hot Ones host Sean Evans were photographed together at a restaurant in New York City, prompting speculation about a possible romantic relationship. The two were seen having dinner at an Italian eatery in what observers described as an intimate setting.

The sighting came months after Palmer and Evans shared a kiss during her appearance on the Hot Ones interview series. The public dinner appearance has intensified rumors about whether the two are dating.

cards.headline: British Royal Family Appears at Trooping the Colour Parade
cards.teaser: The King and Queen and other members of the royal family attended the annual Trooping the Colour military parade in London.
cards.body:
The British royal family gathered at Buckingham Palace for the annual Trooping the Colour ceremony, which marks the King's official birthday. The event featured over 1,400 members of the armed forces and included a Red Arrows flypast watched by the royal family from the palace balcony.

King and Queen received cheers from crowds during the traditional military parade. Prince George, Princess Charlotte, and Prince Louis joined the family on the balcony for the occasion.

hero.headline: US and Iran plan to sign peace framework Sunday
hero.teaser: President Trump said the US and Iran will sign a peace agreement aimed at ending the conflict and easing nuclear tensions.
hero.body:
President Trump announced on Saturday that the United States and Iran plan to sign a peace agreement on Sunday. In a post on Truth Social, Trump stated that the deal would prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping.

"Iran no longer want a Nuclear Weapon, nor will they have one, either through purchase, development, or any other form of procurement," Trump said in his announcement. He added that the strait would open to all shipping immediately after the agreement is signed and suggested that the US relationship with Iran under his administration would be "much different and better one than previous Administrations have had."

However, Iran's foreign ministry cast doubt on the timeline. Esmaeil Baghaei, an Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, cautioned that an exact signing date had not been finalized. "We will have to wait and see about the exact date of the signing of the memorandum of understanding, although it will not be tomorrow," Baghaei said. He noted that signing could potentially happen in the coming days.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed optimism about the negotiations, saying Islamabad was preparing for an electronic signing within 24 hours to be followed by technical-level talks. "We are closer to a peace deal than ever before," Sharif wrote on social media.

The two countries and mediators have been discussing a preliminary peace agreement to end the three-month conflict in the Middle East. However, there are significant disagreements about what the deal contains. According to Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency, the agreement would end conflict on all fronts including Lebanon, release 24 billion dollars of Iran's frozen assets, allow Iran to charge fees for passage through the strait, and suspend sanctions on Iran's oil sales. The agreement would establish a 60-day period for nuclear negotiations.

US officials provided a different account, stating that the deal requires Iran's nuclear material to be destroyed and its nuclear program dismantled. They said Iran's frozen assets would not be released until it meets certain demands and that Iran must stop supporting militant movements in the Middle East.

Trump has repeatedly claimed over the past three months that a deal was imminent. He reserved what he called "the ultimate alternative" if Iran refuses to sign, suggesting continued military action remains possible.

The announcement marks a potential turning point in decades of hostility between Washington and Tehran. The framework addresses multiple sources of tension, including Iran's nuclear program and control of the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and liquid gas supplies previously passed before Iran closed it to most shipping.

cards.headline: White House imposed export controls on Anthropic AI model after Amazon alert
cards.teaser: The White House imposed emergency export controls on Anthropic's advanced AI model after a series of urgent calls between the company's CEO and administration o.
cards.body:
The White House imposed emergency export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models following cybersecurity research from Amazon and conversations between Anthropic CEO Andy Jassy and administration officials. The powerful models had been publicly available for only days before the administration ordered them removed.

The rapid intervention underscores the White House's hands-on approach to managing advanced AI capabilities. The episode marks one of the most direct federal interventions in controlling access to AI technology, with the administration responding to developments as they emerge rather than through established regulatory frameworks.

cards.headline: Trump nominates James McDonald as US Attorney for Manhattan
cards.teaser: President Trump selected James McDonald to lead the Manhattan US Attorney's office, replacing Jay Clayton.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Saturday that he will nominate James McDonald to serve as US Attorney for the Southern District of New York. The move fills the vacancy created by Jay Clayton, who was recently nominated as director of national intelligence.

The Southern District of New York is one of the most prominent federal prosecutor offices in the country, handling high-profile cases involving financial crimes, corruption, and national security matters. McDonald's appointment requires Senate confirmation.

cards.headline: House Democrat criticizes Iran peace deal terms
cards.teaser: Rep. Seth Moulton called the reported Iran agreement a surrender document to Tehran's supreme leader.
cards.body:
Rep. Seth Moulton of Massachusetts criticized the reported Iran peace deal on Saturday, calling it a surrender document. His remarks came after President Trump announced that the US and Iran would sign a peace framework on Sunday.

Both the US and Iran expressed optimism that weeks of negotiations were nearing completion. Trump claimed the deal would prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping. Iran had proposed a different timeline but signaled an agreement was imminent.

cards.headline: Iranian envoy suggests improved US relations if Israel sidelined
cards.teaser: Iran's ambassador to Mexico said the two countries could be friends if the US ignores Israeli interests.
cards.body:
Iran's ambassador to Mexico indicated Friday that Iran and the United States could develop a positive relationship if President Trump does not base his foreign policy on Israeli interests. Ambassador Abolfazl Pasandjdeh said that if the US closes its eyes to Israel's interest, Iran and the US can be very good friends.

The comments come as the two nations prepare to sign a peace framework on Sunday. The statement reflects Iran's longstanding position that American support for Israel represents a major obstacle to improved relations between Washington and Tehran.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from building
cards.teaser: The renowned arts center took down President Trump's name in what officials called a symbolic action.
cards.body:
A federal judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal of President Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade. Work began in the early hours of Saturday, shortly after the performing arts venue missed the court's Friday deadline.

Crews had erected scaffolding on Friday as onlookers gathered, though storms delayed the work until Saturday. The words "The Donald J Trump and" were removed from the building's exterior in the early morning hours behind a screen.

cards.headline: Sen. Cruz backs candidates opposing Trump endorsements
cards.teaser: The Texas senator endorsed rivals to Trump-backed candidates in Georgia and South Carolina governor races.
cards.body:
Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas announced endorsements this week for Republican primary candidates running against President Trump's preferred picks. Cruz backed Rick Jackson for Georgia governor and Alan Wilson for South Carolina governor, both running against Trump-endorsed opponents.

The endorsements mark a break from Trump as Cruz positions himself for a possible 2028 presidential run. Cruz is testing whether the Republican Party will support a potential candidate willing to diverge from Trump, who has maintained control over the party for the past decade.
